newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria natbank head says EMU must start on time.
newsitem.headline: Austria natbank head says EMU must start on time.

text.p: Austrian National Bank President Klaus Liebscher said on Wednesday that Europe's planned single currency must be introduced on schedule in 1999.

"I assume that the single currency will be realised according to plan," Liebscher said in an interview with Die Presse daily, reiterating earlier statements in which he has spoken out strongly against any delay.
"(A delay) would not only be against the constitution but would also destroy an enormous amount of confidence and jeopardise the imminent economic upswing," he continued.
Liebscher said there was a 99 percent probability that the euro would be introduced and did not view a starting group of 10 to 11 countries, including Italy, as unrealistic.
Countries must not diverge too much from the the Maastricht Treaty criteria but there was some room for manoeuvre, he said.
"The figure of 3.0 percent is not in there, the key thing is sustainable consolidation of state finances," he was quoted as saying.
Austria considers itself one of the prime candidates for qualifying for the single currency at its inception.

Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said last week that Austria's overall budget deficit would reach 3.0 percent of gross domestic product this year, putting the country on course for the starting group of Europe's single currency. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
